title: New era of Sri Lankan rugby begins with ‘The Next XV’ | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 03:45
-     - 0

From left: Official F&B Partner Food Studio Director Nadeem Rajabdeen, Official Outdoor Media Partner Richardson Media Head of Sales Kaveesha Hettiarachchi, Official Production Partner KSN Managing Director Ishara Gooneratne, Official Broadcast Partner PEO TV Senior Deputy General Manager – Media Vijitha Bandara, Sri Lanka Rugby President Pavithra Fernando, Sri Lanka Rugby Deputy President/Sponsorship Committee Chairperson Shanitha Fernando, Sri Lanka Schools Rugby President Buddhika Attanayake, Eventistry Sports Founder Karin Wijeratne Powered By Partner, SLT-Mobitel General Manager – Marketing Services Anuruddha Suriarachchi, Official Radio Partner E FM EBC Radio Channel Head Thoshan Ediriweera, Title Partner Euromotors Deputy General Manager Akthar Rizvi and Official Hospitality Partner Hotel City of Dreams Manager Roshan George

Sri Lanka Rugby President Pavithra Fernando

Sri Lankan school rugby is set to enter the franchise era with the launch of The Next XV, a groundbreaking new competition bringing together 140 of the country’s leading schoolboy rugby players across four city-based franchises.

The inaugural league will be played every Saturday from 19 September to 10 October 2026, with double-headers each week and one match played under lights. The first three Saturdays will feature the league stage, followed by the third-place playoff and Grand Final on 10 October.

More than simply another rugby tournament, The Next XV will serve as an official national selection tournament, providing all 140 players with an opportunity to compete under the eyes of national selectors. Each franchise will comprise 35 players, with every player receiving game time during the four-week competition.

The four founding franchises are the Galle Lions, owned by Shamal Perera, Oli Scarr and Dinuk Wijeyaratne; the Colombo Aces, owned by Viren Beruwalage, Saurika Livindu and Thehan Wijemanne; the Kandy Tuskers, owned by Tharanga Gunasekera, Prasad Dissanayake, Shah Doole and Hemanga Karunasena; and the Jaffna Bulls, owned by Udesh Dharmadasa, Prad Navaratnam and Dhovika Seneviratne.

The teams will be led by four respected names in Sri Lankan rugby, with Farzil Marija appointed Head Coach of the Kandy Tuskers, Radhika Hettiarachchi taking charge of the Colombo Aces, Asela Deshapriya leading the Jaffna Bulls and Rohan Chinthaka heading the Galle Lions.

The Next XV is the brainchild of Sri Lanka Rugby President and former player Pavithra Fernando, who believes the league can create a stronger bridge between school rugby and national representation.

“Sri Lanka has never lacked rugby talent. What we have needed is a platform that identifies that talent, gives it national exposure and provides players with a clear opportunity to progress. The Next XV gives 140 young players the chance to step beyond the school jersey, compete alongside the best and show the country what they can do. This is about discovering and developing the players who will shape the future of Sri Lankan rugby,” Fernando said.

Eventistry Sports comes aboard as the Event Rights Holder and Official Marketing, Media and Event Management Partner, bringing its experience in developing and delivering franchise-based sporting properties to school rugby.

“School rugby is one of Sri Lanka’s strongest sporting products, with exceptional talent, tradition and supporter loyalty. The Next XV brings it into the franchise era, combining professional presentation, commercial partnerships, broadcast and fan engagement to unlock greater value and opportunity for the game,” said Karin Wijeratne and Ifham Ariff, Co-Founders of Eventistry Sports, the Event Rights Holder and Official Marketing, Media and Event Management Partner.

All matches will be televised live on PEO SPORTS and streamed on KSN Live, providing nationwide exposure for the players, franchises and competition.

Jetour by Euro Motors joins The Next XV as Title Partner, with SLT-MOBITEL as the Powered By Partner. PEO SPORTS the Broadcast Partner, Sports Nutrition Hub the Hydration Partner, Cinnamon Life the Hospitality Partner, Food Studio the Food & Beverage Partner, Richardson the Outdoor Media Partner and KSN the Production Partner.

While four franchises will contest the inaugural season, plans are already in place to expand The Next XV from its second year, bringing more cities, more players and more opportunities into Sri Lanka’s newest rugby competition.

title: Sri Lanka needs to play more Tests to understand how to play them – Coach Kirsten | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 03:38
-     - 1

Paucity of Test matches is not helping Sri Lanka to develop its Test team

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

Gary Kirsten

Sri Lanka’s head coach Gary Kirsten was critical to the point to say that Sri Lanka is not playing enough Test matches to develop into a team that can challenge other top countries in the format.

Kirsten made these observant comments after Sri Lanka had lost the first Test to India at Galle by 165 runs. This defeat came on the back of a 1-0 (1 drawn) series loss to West Indies in the Caribbean. The two-Test series in the Caribbean in June was played after a gap of one year without a single Test match played.

The contributory factor to this state of affairs is Sri Lanka Cricket’s (SLC) over reliance on white ball cricket than red ball cricket. White ball cricket especially T20I certainly brings in big revenues unlike Test match cricket. However a proper balance must be struck so that red ball cricket is not shunned for the sake of filling the coffers.

Test match cricket is the real form of cricket as compared to the other two formats (T20I and ODI). Players really hone their skills when they play Test cricket. Sadly, SLC seems to have forgotten that important aspect of the game.

“The Sri Lanka team needs to develop. It is sometimes tough when you don’t play many Test matches to understand how you need to play it,” said Kirsten. “This is our third Test in a couple of months and I’ve seen the team developing, but we need to turn it into performance at some point. There’s a lot of talent around but you need to build the shape of the team, need to get 20 wickets consistently. Bowl teams out with seam, bowl teams out with spin and you need your top six batter that can guarantee big runs other than the first innings. That is still developing. Test match cricket is a very different game compared to the white ball and for us it’s important that we develop that Test match squad.”

Speaking further Kirsten said: “The challenge for the modern players especially in Sri Lanka is that we don’t play much Test matches. We have at least six lined up in the next six months or so. It’s great to get into the Test match game a little bit and then try to score runs, bat for a long period of time and have an influence on the game. Sonal (Dinusha) has done that a few times in the West Indies where under pressure he was able to make performances.”

“It’s a big step up between first-class and international level and I thought Sonal handled the pressure of international cricket in his four Test matches exceptionally well. He’s got good mental strength, courage and resilience and he is a good example for all other players. That step up you’ve got to be on your game mentally to manage it.”

“India did apply themselves in that first innings. Dev Padikkal played one of the better Test match innings I’ve seen. He didn’t play too aggressively but played within himself and batted for a long period. It was a good lesson for any Test match batsman how to go and make a big hundred.”

title: ‘The Next XV’: SLR charts new pathway  towards 2035 World Cup | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 03:35
-     - 1

From left: Dinuk de S. Wijeratne (Galle Lions), Thehan Wijemanne (Colombo Aces), Pavithra Fernando (SLR President), Tharanga Gunasekera (Kandy Tuskers) and Tharinda Ratwatte (Jaffna Bulls)

By Shamseer Jaleel

Sri Lanka Rugby (SLR) launched a new pathway towards the 2035 World Cup with the unveiling of four franchise teams for next month’s Junior Under-19 outfits in preparation for the Dec. 2026 Junior Asiad, which will be staged in Sri Lanka.

Sri Lanka Rugby President Pavithra Fernando said ‘The Next XV’ Rugby League is a major new initiative aimed at building a structured pathway for the country’s most promising young players and laying the foundation for the long-term “Road to Rugby World Cup 2035” programme.

Speaking at the official launch press conference, Fernando said ‘The Next XV’ is far more than a tournament, with 140 of Sri Lanka’s leading Under-19 players entering a professionally managed competition where their performances, fitness, technical ability, discipline and character will be assessed over a sustained period.

The players will be distributed among four franchise teams through a structured draft, ensuring competitive balance and giving every player a genuine opportunity to perform. Selection for the national Under-19 pathway will be based on performance, commitment, discipline, fitness and teamwork rather than reputation, school or past achievements.

Fernando stressed that the immediate target is success at the Asia Rugby Under-19 Championship in Colombo during December 2026, with qualification for the World Rugby Under-20 Championship as the key objective. He added that the wider vision is to retain talented players after school and develop them towards senior international rugby.

He also highlighted player welfare and education, while calling for unity beyond school, province or background. “’The Next XV’ represents that commitment. Today, we are not merely launching a competition. We are creating opportunities. We are building a pathway,” Fernando said, underlining the ambition to create a stronger future for Sri Lankan rugby.

title: CCC continues title defence with third straight win | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 03:30
-     - 1

CCC skipper Pavan Rathnayake scored 69 off 63 balls

Sampath Nishshanka ran through the Panadura SC batting taking 5/38

CCC continued their defence of the Major Clubs Limited Overs title when they beat Ace Capitals CC by 43 runs at De Zoysa Stadium, Moratuwa yesterday to secure their third straight win and consolidate their position at the top of Group A.

CCC defended their moderate score of 225-9 by bowling out Ace Capital CC for 182 with their spinners capturing all ten wickets. Ashian Daniel had the best figures with 3/30 and was supported by Dilum Sudeera, Rashmika Hirushan and Lasith Croospulle with two wickets each. There were only two half-centuries scored in the entire match – by skipper Pavan Rathnayake (69 off 63 balls, 4 fours, 3 sixes) for CCC and Thisara Ekanayake (63 off 112 balls, 2 fours) for Ace Capitals CC.

Following defeats in their first two games Nugegoda SWC finally broke the losing trend by registering their first win beating Panadura SC by a thumping margin of 157 runs (DLS method) at Thurstan grounds. Rehan Peiris (57 off 77 balls, 4 fours, 2 sixes) and Sammu Ashan (85 off 104 balls, 8 fours, 1 six) shared a third wicket stand of 102 for Nugegoda SWC to post a score of 278-7. Panadura SC had their target revised to 273 from 41 overs but they crumbled for 115 to the left-arm medium-pace of Sampath Nishshanka who finished with figures of 5/38. (ST)

title: Hashan Tillakaratne appointed Batting Coach of Senior Men’s Program | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 22 August 2026 03:26
-     - 0

Hashan Tillakaratne

Sri Lanka Cricket has appointed Hashan Tillakaratne as the Batting Coach of the Senior Men’s Program.

He will be based at the National High Performance Center of the SLC and will work with the national players as part of the Senior Men’s Program.

The former World Cup winner previously served as the batting coach of the Sri Lanka men's national team and as head coach of the Sri Lanka women's national team.

He has also served as the head coach of the Bangladesh women’s national team.

Tillakaratne represented Sri Lanka from 1989 to 2003, playing 83 Test matches and 200 ODIs accumulating more than 8,200 international runs across the two formats. His appointment came into effect on 20 August and will continue until 31st December 2027.

Sri Lanka will make a significant contribution to the Asia Rugby Sevens Series 2026, with Ishanka Abeykoon appointed as a referee and experienced official Dilroy Fernando named Referee Manager for the opening round in Suzhou, China, from 29 to 30 August.

The appointments underline Sri Lanka’s growing contribution to the development of match officiating within Asian rugby, with both officials playing important roles at the region’s premier annual sevens competition.

Abeykoon is among the selected referees and assistant referees drawn from across Asia, joining officials from Japan, Hong Kong China, Singapore, China, Taipei, Thailand, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE. He is an old boy of Nugawela Central.

Fernando, who has extensive experience in Asian rugby officiating, will oversee the referee management team and play a key role in ensuring high standards throughout the tournament, carrying much pride for Isipathana College as an old boy.

The Suzhou round will feature 24 leading men’s and women’s national teams competing over two days. (SJ)
